function: Per-UAV distributed Q-learning picks the served ground terminal and discrete transmit power to maximize energy efficiency; a CRLB-based sensing prior initializes the Q-table (p. 5, 8).
system: M=12 aerial base stations (UAVs, 200 m) serve L=10 ground terminals at 2.6 GHz, 20 MHz; scalar LoS gain, antennas not stated, no RIS (p. 3, 4, 9).
method: Independent tabular Q-learning per UAV (multi-agent, epsilon-greedy, discount 0.5), trained online; Q-table initialized by an improved FBSS subset selection based on CRLB (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS free-space air-to-ground gain (exponent 2), fixed random ground terminal positions, predefined UAV paths, Gaussian TDOA noise; no dataset (p. 3, 4, 9).
test_conditions: Single scenario (M=12, L=10), online learning and evaluation in it; 100 Monte Carlo runs; exploration factors 0.2, 0.5, 0.9; no new-condition test (p. 9-12).
baselines: Naive random decisions, FBSS [38] for UAV subset selection, and Q-learning without the sensing prior; no earlier learned method (p. 9-12).
metrics: Total reward and energy efficiency of UAVs (throughput per power), improvement over random, positioning accuracy (m), PDF/CCDF over 100 Monte Carlo runs (p. 10-12).
complexity: none (only qualitative remarks on computing cost, p. 7, 8)
q1_support: p. 3: "the channel power gain of LoS between UAV-m and GT-l follows the free space propagation model"; a custom scalar LoS model, with no 3GPP model, public dataset or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "it is necessary to re-assign the initial value of the Q-table for each UAV agent according to the above method"; the Q-table is re-initialized in each sensing interval, and only one scenario (M=12, L=10, p. 9) is evaluated.
q3_support: p. 9: "a random method according to some specific constraints is selected as the benchmark comparison in our research"; FBSS [38] is also non-learned, and no earlier learned method or standard RL baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 7: "considering saving computing resources and accelerating convergence speed"; this is qualitative, and no order of complexity, operation count, parameter count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 9: "Table I summarizes the key simulation parameters used in this section"; custom simulation, no code or data link, and no public dataset.
notes: Included in area 6 (UAV aerial links: learned transmit power and ground-terminal selection, physical layer under step 1); ISAC area 5 also fits but 6 is more specific. If the reviewer picks area 5, the scalar single-antenna link with no RIS (p. 3, 4) would hit the system exclusion. Table I read from the page image (p. 9). The sensing prior comes from a non-learned FBSS heuristic.
